ASPIRE releases version 1.0 with robot skill refinement and stronger simulation results

The open-source project reports gains after a backbone-model change; simulation scores must be separated from hardware performance.

Robotics Weekly ↗16 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryVideos 1

A reusable skill library

ASPIRE version 1.0 provides an agent framework for discovering and refining robot skills, storing reusable knowledge in a skill library. Its GitHub project lists new Rubik’s Cube capability and real-robot learning.

Scores have a defined scope

The team reports about 99% on 80 LIBERO-Pro tasks and 100% on seven representative Robosuite tasks and two BEHAVIOR-1K tasks after switching to GPT-6 Astra. These are simulation scores, not universal real-world robot success rates.

Open code and hardware questions

Researchers can inspect the code and examples. Hardware demonstrations indicate a direction for skill refinement, but the report provides no hardware success-rate suite comparable with the simulation scores. Physical deployment still needs machine-appropriate constraints and supervision.
